newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Slump on Wall Street drags down ADRs.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Slump on Wall Street drags down ADRs.

text.p: Shares of American Depositary Receipts were mixed in lackluster trading on Wednesday as foreign stocks followed Wall Street's slide, traders said.

"I think that confusion reigns," said Val Kosmider, head of international equity trading at Schroder Wertheim. "The performance of yesterday's market here was not very impressive and that has left people scratching their heads."
He said the dollar's rally on Tuesday and the moderate growth outlined in the Beige Book released by the Federal Reserve earlier today also are influencing the ADR market.
Royal Dutch Petroleum Co, which was carried higher on the dollar's rise on Tuesday, shed 1-7/8 to trade at 164-1/8 as the dollar pulled back from 23-month highs in Europe.
Other energy companies also slipped, including British Petroleum Co Plc which dropped 2-1/8 to 134-1/8 and France's Total SA which shed 1/2 to trade at 40-1/4.
Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson fell 3/8 to 30, Glaxo Wellcome Plc dropped 1/2 to 31-1/4 and Reuters Holdings Plc shed 2-1/4 at 68-3/8.
Latin American ADR shares also followed the Dow which slid over 27 points in midday activity to 6415, a trader said.
"I think they are catching up a little bit on the Dow. We have a combination of profit taking and catch up," she said.
Grupo Televisa SA de CV fell 1/8 to 27-1/8 and YPF SA shed 1/4 to 23.
Blue-chip telecommunication stocks held firm. Brazil's Telebras traded in line at 77-1/2 and Mexico's Telmex gained 1/8 to 31-1/2.
